title: Service Resilience Roadshow and Ops Ramp Plan
content:
Purpose:
This doc outlines a cross-functional program to raise baseline service resilience across product teams through a structured roadshow, SLO adoption ramp, and ops enablement runbooks. Goal: get 6 critical services to 99.9% availability SLO or equivalent error-budget policies and onboard 10+ service teams into the measurement + remediation loop by end of Q3 2026.

Executive summary:
- Problem: Many product services lack consistent SLI measurement, heterogeneous alerting, and no common playbooks for degradation.
- Proposal: A 12-week program of roadshow sessions + hands-on SLO clinics + unblock sprints with the SRE guild supporting each team.
- Outcome: measurably improved SLI coverage, standardized runbooks, and reduced mean time to restore (MTTR) for incidents tied to the targeted SLOs.

Scope and in-scope services:
- In-scope: API gateway, chat-generation service, embeddings-indexer, model-routing, billing-sync, dedicated-queue-manager (initial six).
- Out-of-scope for first wave: experimental research endpoints, internal analytics pipelines (to be considered in later waves).

Success criteria (measurable):
- Each targeted service has a working SLI dashboard reporting availability and latency within our telemetry (95th/99th latency and availability).
- SLOs defined and approved for each service (example: availability 99.9% monthly, p95 latency 300ms).
- Runbook and on-call playbook checked into repo and linked in Confluence.
- Incident play simulation completed for each service and action items closed.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Program lead: Maya Chen (eng-sre) — coordination, reporting, exec updates.
- SLO SMEs: Riley Morgan, Samira Ortiz — measurement, alert thresholds.
- Observability infra: Lukas Bauer — dashboard templates, metrics onboarding.
- Product reps: Product owners for each service (see annex).
- Solutions Eng & SEs: provide customer-facing impact context and prioritization.

High-level timeline (12 weeks):
- Week 0 (planning): Program kickoff, invite list, baseline metrics snapshot, create tracking board (JIRA-ENG-4721).
- Weeks 1-4 (Roadshow wave 1): 2-hour session per service: overview + hands-on telemetry bootcamp + SLO draft.
- Weeks 5-8 (Ops ramp & sprints): Focused two-week sprints to fix gaps (instrumentation, alerts, dashboards, RBAC).
- Weeks 9-10 (Runbooks & drills): Author runbooks, run tabletop exercise with on-call.
- Weeks 11-12 (Wrap & handoff): Final audits, exec summary, commitments for wave 2.

Sprint map (example):
- Sprint A (W1-W2): API gateway onboarding — add availability SLI, alerting rule, dashboard.
- Sprint B (W3-W4): Chat-generation service — implement p95/p99 latency histograms and cache-miss SLI.
- Sprint C (W5-W6): Embeddings-indexer — tune retries, backpressure metrics, error-budget policy.
- Sprint D (W7-W8): Model-routing & queue-manager — autoscaling and graceful-failover tests.

SLO design notes (per service):
- Principle: prefer simple, customer-facing SLI first (availability/latency) then secondary indicators (error-rate, queue-depth).
- Measurement windows: 30d rolling for availability; 7d for alerting evaluation.
- Alerting policy: page at 5% of daily error-budget burn in 1h OR sustained p99 latency breach over 10m.
- Budget: express in monthly error-budget tokens; document expected false positive rate tolerance.

Operational playbooks to deliver:
- On-call pager flow (who to page when SLO breach detected).
- Triage checklist (first 15 minutes): verify telemetry, scope blast radius, rollback decisions.
- Escalation matrix and communication templates (Slack channel, status page blurb).
- Post-incident review template with SLO impact calculation.

Training and enablement:
- Roadshow sessions: 90m slide + 30m hands-on in staging with telemetry examples.
- Office hours: twice-weekly drop-in for 6 weeks during ramp.
- Asynchronous material: recording + step-by-step SLI onboarding doc + one-click dashboard template.

Telemetry and infra dependencies:
- Required: metrics emitted (request_success, request_latency_ms buckets, queue_depth), traces with service names.
- Work needed: add p99 histograms, ensure tags: region, model-version, route.
- Infra tickets: OBS-4850 (histogram lib upgrade), INF-998 (reduce retention gaps).

Risk register and mitigations (top items):
- Risk: Teams lack bandwidth for instrumentation. Mitigation: SRE squad offers 2-day embedded pairing per team; prioritize minimal SLI set.
- Risk: Too many alert storms. Mitigation: conservative default thresholds, error-budget based paging.
- Risk: Telemetry gaps cause false negatives. Mitigation: pre-flight checklist and telemetry smoke tests before each roadshow session.

Communications plan:
- Weekly sync email to execs with progress + one-pager metrics snapshot.
- Roadshow invite posted in #sre-roadshow slack and includes checklist.
- Post-mortem and templates stored under Confluence link above.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should we centralize SLO storage in the console or maintain per-team YAMLs? (decision due by Week 2)
- Are model-variant level SLOs required immediately or can we roll them into wave 2?

Quick action list (first 2 weeks):
- Create program JIRA board and invite reps (owner: Maya).
- Baseline metrics export for 6 services (owner: Lukas).
- Draft SLO templates for availability and latency (owner: Riley).
- Schedule roadshow slots and create calendar invites (owner: Samira).

Annex: example SLO template (text):
- Service: <service-name>
- Customer-facing indicator: success rate of 2xx/3xx requests for production traffic
- SLI measurement: rolling 30d availability computed from request_success metric
- Objective: 99.9% monthly availability
- Alerting: page when 5% of monthly error-budget consumed in 60 minutes
- Runbook link: <confluence-url>/runbooks/<service-name>

Notes to self:
- Keep sessions pragmatic — engineering teams respond better to hands-on fixes than long slides.
- Capture screenshots of dashboards during sessions for playbook examples.
- Track writeups for each service as a single source of truth in the repo.

Next steps:
- Approve scope and finalize calendar by Feb 26 2026.
- Begin outreach to product area leads and schedule first session for API gateway week of Mar 9.

-- end --
